implementation_notes: In .NET the sprawl template is one ASP.NET Core project per entity, because the project template is the obvious starting point and each project is deployable by construction. Each brings its own `Program.cs`, its own DI container, its own configuration binding, its own middleware pipeline and its own container image. The detection is the solution file and the container registry; the consolidation is one host with several assemblies, which keeps the DI container and the middleware pipeline singular while the internal boundaries remain explicit. The .NET-specific sprawl cost is the startup memory footprint multiplied by the service count, which matters on serverless pricing.
idiom_name: ASP.NET Core project per domain noun
pitfalls: Each host brings its own middleware pipeline, so a cross-cutting concern (auth, logging, correlation) is N edits rather than one.
Multiple containers mean multiple base images to patch, which multiplies the CVE surface by the service count.
`IHttpClientFactory` and resilience middleware configured per service means the retry policy is N policies that drift.
